content:
- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in the first 10–15 days of the forecast horizon.
- Forecast shows early overshoots after sharp spikes in history (e.g., 74+), then gradually declines — but true values often remain higher or stabilize later.
- Model fails to capture mean reversion in the short term; true values often revert to mid-range after initial spikes.
- Forecast tends to be flat or slightly increasing, while true values show more volatility and occasional sharp drops.
- Model overestimates near the end of the forecast horizon, especially when true values are trending downward.
- Forecast lags behind true values by 1–3 days in the early part of the horizon, then catches up or diverges.
- Model ignores recent low values in history when forecasting, leading to persistent overestimation.
- True values often dip below forecast mid-horizon, suggesting model is too optimistic in the middle of the forecast window.
